profile.summary: A single-centre study that reclassified 450 BRCA1 missense variants with conflicting ClinVar interpretations (ClinVar accessed 20 December 2022) with two methods: the automated VarSome tool and manual curation under the CanVIG-UK BRCA1/BRCA2 gene-specific guidance. It reports how often the two agree on a three-class scale, and how each matches ClinVar submitters and the 17 variants that later reached a ClinVar consensus. It is relevant to clinical variant scientists choosing between automated and gene-specific classification.

sections.title: What it measures
sections.body: How much an automated ACMG classifier (VarSome premium v11.5) and gene-specific manual curation (CanVIG-UK BRCA1/BRCA2 guidance v1.17) agree on BRCA1 missense variants that ClinVar submitters disagree about, and how each relates to ClinVar submitter calls and later ClinVar consensus.

quotes.text: The tier classification of each variant was determined using VarSome premium (v11.5), an automated variant interpretation tool that applies the ACMG guidelines
CanVIG-UK gene-specific guidance (v1.17) by a genetic specialist at our institution
We evaluated the proportions of VarSome and CanVIG-UK classifications in relation to the ClinVar submitter results

sections.title: How it is built
sections.body: Of 12,719 BRCA1 variants in ClinVar on 20 December 2022, 654 had conflicting interpretations, and the 450 missense variants among them were analysed. CanVIG-UK classifications were made by one genetic specialist and cross-checked by a second; VarSome results were used as produced, with no manual change. The same 450 variants were re-extracted from ClinVar on 1 May 2024 to find any that had reached consensus.

sections.title: Evaluation methodology
sections.body: The five classes are merged into three (PV/LPV, VUS, BV/LBV). The main result is overall concordance between the two methods: 58.9% (95% CI 52.0 to 66.4%; 265/450), with no PV/LPV versus BV/LBV disagreements. Secondary analyses compare each method's calls with the share of ClinVar submitters calling a variant pathogenic or benign, and with the 17 variants (3.8%) that had a ClinVar consensus by May 2024; each method disagreed with that consensus on one variant.

quotes.text: To facilitate a more coherent comparison, the five classifications were consolidated into three broad categories: PV/LPV, VUS, and BV/LBV.
The overall concordance rate was 58.9% (95% CI: 52.0–66.4%; 265/450) between VarSome and CanVIG-UK
No variants classified as PV/LPV in VarSome were classified as BV/LBV in CanVIG-UK or vice versa.
Further analysis of the 450 conflicting variants in ClinVar on 1 May 2024 showed that 17 variants (3.8%) had reached a consensus (9 PV/LPV, 1 VUS, and 7 BV/LBV).
The variant classifications of VarSome and CanVIG-UK were in agreement with the final ClinVar consensus for all but one variant each

facts.label: Assays
facts.value: No new assay. Labels are ClinVar submitter classifications; the classification rules draw on population frequency, published functional studies, REVEL or MetaRNN predictions and multifactorial likelihood data.

quotes.text: we applied PP3 and BP4 criteria for protein impact evaluation using the meta-predictor REVEL

VarSome integrates data from multiple sources, including population databases, such as gnomAD with specific frequency thresholds and functional prediction algorithms, such as MetaRNN for missense variants

facts.label: Allowed inputs
facts.value: Inapplicable: these are classification tools and guidelines applied to evidence, not prediction models given a fixed input.

facts.label: Adaptation
facts.value: Inapplicable: no model is trained or adapted.
